title: FounderGate Checker Anti-Trust Veto Checklist
description: A checker can look reliable by nailing the CHEAP metrics — fast reviews, few loops, low false-positive — while a disqualifying condition (it misses real defects, or its verdict flaps on re-run) hides underneath. Each veto below is HARD: if it triggers, the disposition is forced to UNRELIABLE and the effective band to red regardless of the numeric band. Each warning is SOFT: it flags friction/risk without failing the checker. The scorer (score.mjs) enforces these; this file is the human-auditable copy of the same rules, and the selftest asserts the id-sets match so this copy cannot silently drift.

vetoes.why: A checker that passes one in five real, labelled defects as clean is worse than no checker — it manufactures false confidence. No aggregate can buy that back.
A verdict that flips PASS/FAIL on re-run of the same input is not a verdict; it is a coin flip and cannot be trusted or reproduced.
When more than half a checker's findings are spurious it trains every reviewer to ignore it, so its real catches get ignored too — it is crying wolf.
Five or more review rounds per episode means the checker is stuck in a rework loop rather than converging on a verdict.

warnings.why: A quarter or more spurious findings is friction that erodes reviewer trust before it reaches the veto threshold.
Even a single missed defect below the veto line is worth surfacing — a miss is never routine for a checker.
Rare re-run drift is tolerable but should be watched; it can grow into flapping.
A median review over two minutes delays every downstream lane waiting on the verdict.
Three or four loops per episode is elevated rework churn short of the thrash veto.
A rate measured over fewer than 20 episodes is not yet statistically trustworthy; treat the score as provisional.
